transcript: If you had very reactive parents when you were a little kid, that can shape the way your nervous system works for the rest of your life. And here's why. If you grew up with a parent who exploded over small mistakes or reacted harshly to normal childhood behaviors, your nervous system learned to stay on high alert, a sharp tone, a slammed cabinet, a spilled cup, a simple mistake. To a child, these things can feel much bigger than they appear, so your body adapts. It learns to stay alert, to watch every expression, to predict every reaction, to avoid making mistakes at all costs. Over time, your nervous system becomes trained to expect danger, even when no danger is present. You may find yourself overthinking a simple message before sending it, apologizing for things that are not your fault, feeling anxious when someone's mood changes slightly, not because you are weak, not because something is wrong with you, but because your nervous system is still trying to protect the child you once were. The mind lives in the present, but the nervous system often lives in the past. That is why healing is not about controlling every thought. It is about teaching your body that the danger is no longer here, slowly, patiently, with compassion. The storm has passed, and your nervous system can learn safety again. If these words resonate with you, I share more lessons on healing, inner peace, and understanding yourself in my book. You can find it in the link on my profile.
